name: Visa-free tourist entry (Mercosur and associated states)
summary: Citizens of Mercosur members and associated states can enter as tourists without a visa for up to 90 days. Since DNU 366/2025, entrants declare their purpose and say they hold health insurance.

other: Art. 34 of the migration law, as changed by DNU 366/2025, asks you to file a sworn statement of your purpose and say you have health insurance.
This list is only for the countries named on the official tourist page. Other nationalities may also be visa-free, so check the official visa lookup.

name: Visa-free entry for Chinese, Indian and Dominican nationals with a US visa
summary: Citizens of China, India or the Dominican Republic who hold a valid US visa or green card can enter as tourists without an Argentine visa for up to 90 days.

name: Tourist visa or AVE electronic authorization
summary: Nationals who are not visa-free need a tourist visa from an Argentine consulate. Some nationalities can get an electronic travel authorization (AVE) instead, if the official lookup shows it is enabled for them.

other: Check your nationality in the official Migraciones visa lookup linked from the tourist page.
Visa-free lists, AVE rules, business visit and airside transit rules were not confirmed from an official page, so this record needs review.

name: Transitory Residence for Digital Nomads
summary: For remote independent workers with clients abroad. Initial residence is up to 180 days and can be extended for the same period. Only open to nationals of countries that don't need a tourist visa.

other: Must work remotely as an independent professional for clients domiciled abroad.
No minimum income is set. You show proof of activity such as a contract, company endorsement, certifications or income receipts.
Nationals of countries that need a tourist visa are not eligible.
The extension needs proof of income earned during the residence period plus a criminal record from your home country.

sources.label: Digital nomad visa, Argentine Consulate Toronto

stay.note: Can be extended for the same period.

documents: Argentine criminal record certificate (via RaDEX, age 16+)
Signed application note on your independent work
Proof of work activity and at least one work reference
steps: The process is in person, not through RaDEX. In Buenos Aires city, email Migraciones. Elsewhere, go to your local Migraciones office.
Pay fees through the platform and bring original documents with apostilles and Spanish translations.
processing: The Toronto consulate page says its online TIE 24H option usually takes about 10 to 15 business days with a complete file. Applying through a consulate is also possible.

name: Temporary Residence as Rentista or Pensionado
summary: For people with stable foreign investment income (rentista) or a foreign pension (pensionado). Temporary residence is up to 3 years. The pension extension is 1 year at a time.

other: Rentista: stable monthly income for at least two years, no less than 5 times the national minimum wage (SMVM).
Pensionado: pension from a government, international organization or private company for services abroad, at least 5 times the SMVM per month.
The pages give the threshold as a multiple of the SMVM, not a peso amount. Check the current SMVM value.

sources.label: Entry permit as rentista or pensionado (argentina.gob.ar)

documents: Rentista: certificate from the remitting entity showing where the funds come from
Pensionado: copy of the pension grant and last three pay slips
Signed request letter and passport copy
steps: An attorney with power of attorney files the request with Migraciones (Tramitación de Ingresos).
Migraciones decides, then you apply for the visa at an Argentine consulate.

name: Temporary Residence by Mercosur Nationality
summary: Citizens of Mercosur and associated states can get 2-year temporary residence, renewable, with no job offer or income test listed. This is the Mercosur free-residence route.

other: Also open to people naturalized for at least 5 years in Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador or Peru who are native citizens of another country.
Applications for most residences run through RaDEX (migraciones.gob.ar/radex). You must be inside Argentina and file in person once invited.
Work rights are not stated on the page.

documents: Valid passport or Mercosur travel document
Criminal record certificates from countries where you lived over a year in the last 3 years

name: Temporary Residence as Migrant Worker
summary: For employees with a pre-employment contract from an Argentine employer. 1 year, renewable. The employer must be registered with ARCA and the migration authority's requester registry.

other: Pay must follow the applicable collective agreement.
Employer submits the ARCA early registration (alta temprana) within 30 calendar days of starting the application.
Applications for most residences run through RaDEX (migraciones.gob.ar/radex). You must be inside Argentina and file in person once invited.

documents: Pre-employment contract signed by both parties, signatures certified
Proof of address and regular entry

name: Temporary Residence as Student
summary: For regular students at recognized secondary, tertiary, university or specialized schools, plus interns and scholarship holders. 1 year, renewable.

other: Interns and scholars also need an international agreement or acceptance letter.
Electronic enrollment confirmation from the school is required.
Work rights are not stated on the page.
DNU 366/2025 changed higher education rules for foreigners. Check fee and access rules with your university.

name: Temporary Residence by Family Reunification
summary: For spouses, parents and children of Argentine citizens, and spouses, parents and minor children of temporary or permanent residents. Lasts as long as the sponsor's residence, up to 3 years if the sponsor is Argentine or permanent.

other: Spouse, parent or child of an Argentine citizen.
Spouse, parent, unmarried child under 18 or adult child with a disability of a resident.
Legalized birth or marriage certificate proving the link.
Applications for most residences run through RaDEX (migraciones.gob.ar/radex). You must be inside Argentina and file in person once invited.

stay.note: Matches the sponsor's residence, up to 3 years for Argentine or permanent sponsors.

name: Permanent Residence
summary: After 2 years of temporary residence for Mercosur nationals or 3 years for others, if you can show means to live in Argentina. Also open to children of Argentines born abroad, recognized refugees, Brazilians and ex-diplomats.

other: You must have spent at least 50% of the granted period in Argentina and not been abroad 6 or more consecutive months.
Proof of sufficient means of subsistence and no criminal record that justifies rejection (Art. 22, as changed by DNU 366/2025).
Permanent residents can use the public health system like citizens. Others need insurance or pre-payment under the new Art. 8.
Residence can be cancelled after 1 year outside Argentina.

name: Naturalization (2-year residence route)
summary: Adults can apply after 2 years of legal, continuous residence. DNU 366/2025 added that you can't leave the country at all during those 2 years. Check before you plan trips.

other: Legal and continuous residence for the 2 years before applying.
Per the DNU summary, continuity means no trips abroad in that period.
Language and test requirements were not confirmed from an official page.
Dual citizenship rules were not confirmed from an official page.

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship not confirmed from an official source. DNU 366/2025 changed Ley 346,.

name: Citizenship by Investment (announced)
summary: DNU 366/2025 created a route for people who make a relevant investment, no matter how long they have lived in Argentina. A new agency under the Ministry of Economy will assess applications. The investment amount and rules were not confirmed.

other: The Ministry of Economy defines what counts as a relevant investment.
No amount or opening date was found on an official page. Treat as not open until confirmed.
